ruleset.name: CWE-89 / CWE-22 syntactic sinks
ruleset.description: Hand-authored PMD XPath rules targeting SQL Injection (CWE-89) and Path Traversal (CWE-22). PMD has no taint/dataflow engine, so these are PURELY SYNTACTIC: they flag a known sink whose argument is not a string literal. This deliberately over-approximates (flags sanitized calls too), illustrating the high-false-positive failure mode of rule-based SAST that the hybrid LLM-confirmer stage is designed to mitigate. NOT stock PMD.

rule.name: SqlInjectionConcatExec
rule.message: Possible SQL Injection (CWE-89): non-literal argument to a JDBC execute method.
rule.description: Flags execute/executeQuery/executeUpdate/prepareStatement called with anything other than a direct string literal.

rule.name: PathTraversalFileSink
rule.message: Possible Path Traversal (CWE-22): non-literal path passed to a file-system sink.
rule.description: Flags File / FileInputStream / FileReader / RandomAccessFile (and write variants) constructed with anything other than a string literal.
